title: test(work-items): cover packaged browser session denial and recovery
body:
The native Work Items browser harness now removes its own session cookie, requires a real middleware 403, verifies the protected page returns to the API-key sign-in screen, and reauthenticates to read the existing item. The exact build-input assets archive was recovered from the verified Go binary's embedded byte range and matched the original manifest hash; it was not rebuilt.

New-head CI remains required. This changes tests and the Work Items guide only, and does not close #208. Go-wrapper execution for this new denial case, generic HTTP 500, missing support, actual crash recovery, accessibility, non-Chromium and actual ChatGPT acceptance remain NOT RUN. title: fix: preserve database state when nested SAVEPOINT creation fails
body:
When SQLite rejects creation of a nested SAVEPOINT, the nesting count was incremented before acquisition succeeded. Outer cleanup then masked the original database error with an assertion and left the connection's transaction bookkeeping unusable. Increment the count only after SAVEPOINT creation succeeds.

The regression uses SQLite's real authorizer to deny SAVEPOINT/BEGIN, verifies the original error and that the nested body never runs, then commits another nested transaction on the same connection. The canonical operations guide records this failure boundary.

title: fix: preserve concrete MCP resource owners across catalog changes
body:
A concrete MCP resource URI could change owners when the catalog moved between direct resources and overlapping resource templates, even after #289 reserved exact keys. Three deterministic regressions fail on the affected d3c27137 source and pass this candidate.

This adds migration14 and bounded, canonical history of admitted resource routing. It preserves the existing direct-resource precedence and template matcher. Before invoking a resource callback, the current winner is compared with historical winners; a changed logical package/action owner is rejected. History shares the existing catalog admission lock/transaction, survives restart, rolls back with failed admission, deduplicates unchanged projections, and fails closed on malformed history or exceeded limits. Protective records are never evicted. Renaming to a non-conflicting route is required; rediscovery alone cannot authorize a reassigned URI.

Merge dependency: #289. Related: #279, #101, #129, #130, #135. #89 remains closed. This is a legacy catalog correctness repair, separate from Package v3 or authorization grants.

Validation:
- 24 new cases; 73 affected tests, 115 MCP tests and 19 schema/SQL boundary tests passed; configured lint/types and migration0→14 golden parity passed.
- Independent PostgreSQL17 acceptance: seven checks passed, covering fresh/migrated schema parity, retained metadata, long route keys, no-op admission, changed-owner rejection, transaction rollback, capacity limits, and two-process admission.
- Independent source review approved author444349/tree d9174bf. Combined publication tree768ec7b also independently reviewed; its only added change is #289's test-child diagnostics. Author/source and actual published ancestry are preserved.

Current head5ebc97c has tree768ec7bb91f0636c17440d2920c0db1d84a93ec4. Local444349→published2f84fd2; reviewed local merge4ac8f180→published5ebc97c, parents[2f84fd2,2116a36].

Remaining gates: hosted checks on the published candidate, any resulting Windows diagnostic repair, freshly built native artifact and affected acceptance, and final combined integration review. Older c782 native evidence does not prove this production change. The existing regex language is preserved; bounds limit storage and route iteration, not regex CPU. Pre-upgrade routing history is unrecoverable. An unavailable resource is not forwarded to an old implementation.

Canonical repository operations guidance documents migration, matching, admission/read behavior, limits, and recovery. Upstream disposition: Actions-local defect, no external report. No publication or whole-issue completion is claimed.

title: Integrate Actions Runtime 1.0.3 security, execution, and native acceptance work
body:
Converges the existing Actions Runtime/community foundation into `community`: multi-package import/reload/catalog repairs, execution and security fixes, Work Items checkpoints, bounded Deployment values, and confined source-reading/staging prerequisites. Current integration is `e886d26ebaefafa9189a69517f6707691b53662e` (tree `016664a8e0d01dec36accf4fe5d39cb0b7bebef7`); community remains `36b8192dbb8143e016af3351f7d25b22a35c9944`. This is a checkpoint in the complete retained issue graph.

Accepted integration now includes #289 historical MCP alias ownership, #297 deterministic frontend benchmark and #298 confined selected-source staging, following independent review and exact-head checks. These merges do not establish whole-issue acceptance or complete-source compilation.

Remaining integration/release gates:
- #292 resource-routing history: independent combined-tree review passed; latest head `d0e12c1e` has 18/19 checks passed, with Windows devmode still running at the 2026-10-10 17:52Z observation. Required checks must finish.
- #290 frozen control: source-pinned run 38070410096 passed eleven Linux native cases and eleven Go-wrapper cases on head `9e1059a1`. Independently replayed evidence binds the older native producer through a strict source-equivalence guard, with one declared unwired staging-module addition. This is not a new final-source native release, other-platform execution, or zero-exit wrapper claim. General exact-head checks and the declared #292 integration dependency remain.
- Finish security, browser/protocol, wheel and platform acceptance on the final combined source. This PR's current thirteen listed checks pass; that does not waive the separately recorded gates or certify newer descendants.
- Publish only through the authorized immutable workflows once their gates pass; independently retrieve registry packages, native binaries and checksums, then update the owning Homebrew distribution and prove installation/upgrade.

Canvas and the full architecture continue in parallel. #282's process-cleanup repair passed hosted regression checks, but its Core1.0.3 dependency contract remains blocked. #291 prepared the Core1.0.3 public-authoring API with clean installed-wheel/provenance evidence; published Core1.0.2 lacks that API. #301's required frontend workflow ran with eight round-trip tests and zero skips plus 280 frontend tests; renderer evidence is separate from real ChatGPT verification. #299/#300 prepare shared authorized output services. #302 is the bounded RCC authoritative identity prerequisite; its new real-RCC three-case proof remains pending.

The 2026-10-10 17:09Z registry observation found Helper1.0.3, Core1.0.2, Runtime1.0.2 and Work Items0.4.4; Core1.0.3 and Runtime1.0.3 were absent. No Runtime1.0.3 GitHub native release exists in that observation; latest is1.0.1. Publication is not claimed.

All54 original contracts remain retained: latest recorded stages are1 accepted/closed,8 integrated-but-unaccepted,8 active,9 review and28 blocked. Source acceptance, integration, full-issue completion and verified distribution are distinct. Cloud work continues. The user deleted Devsy; it stays on HOLD until a new explicit HIT THE GAS and readiness verification. No repository migration is included.
